jurisdiction.name: United Arab Emirates
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The UAE governs AI through federal soft law, sector rules and emirate-level instruments; no AI-specific federal statute has been identified so far. The National Strategy for AI 2031 (2018), the AI Ethics Principles (2022) and the UAE Charter for the Development and Use of AI (2024) set the national direction, and the Personal Data Protection Law (2021) is the main binding federal layer. Sector regulators add more specific rules, including the Central Bank's AI/ML guidance note (2026), the joint financial regulators' enabling-technologies guidelines (2021), the Cyber Security Council's National Cyber Security Policy for AI and Ministry of Education guidance on generative AI in schools. At emirate level, Abu Dhabi set up its Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council by law in 2024 and reorganised it by Law No. (5) of 2025; Dubai and Abu Dhabi regulate AI in health, and in the DIFC, Regulation 10 (2023) governs AI-based processing of personal data and the DIFC Courts issued guidance on generative AI in proceedings (2023), while the ADGM Courts' Practice Direction 2 requires parties to disclose AI use in document searches. The direction is consolidation: in June 2026 the Cabinet approved a federal Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority to merge the AI Office, TDRA's digital government sector and the UAE Data Office; its founding legal text has not been published so far.
lead_institutions: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain
Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority (approved June 2026)
Abu Dhabi Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 6 October 2026, covering federal bodies and the emirates of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, including the Dubai International Financial Centre; some official sites were unavailable, so details of the Cyber Security Council's AI security policy were taken from the government's official policy portal. Some documents are listed as leads to check later until an official text is published, including an autonomous-vehicles law and Abu Dhabi Global Market data protection rules. A follow-up check in October 2026 added Abu Dhabi's laws on its AI and Advanced Technology Council and the DIFC Courts' generative AI guidance; the founding law of the federal Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority is held as a lead, and the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts' disclosure rule on AI searches was added.

instruments.english_title: Safe and Responsible Use Guide of Generative AI in Classrooms
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Education on its AI Literacy page in Arabic and English (cover: 'Ministry of Education 2026'). Applies to all public schools and private schools following the MOE curriculum. Publication date source: year printed on the cover of both language versions.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Education rules for classroom use of generative AI in all public schools and private schools following the MOE curriculum, covering Grades 7-12. It sets guiding principles (equity, teacher empowerment, well-being, transparency and data protection, academic integrity), assigns roles to school leaders, teachers, students, IT staff and parents, bans use by students under 13 or below Grade 7, use in exams and assessments, undisclosed AI-generated work, deepfakes and uploading personal data, and permits only the tools listed in its annex (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude). Breaches are classified as behaviour violations of different degrees, with exam use handled under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2023 and Ministerial Decision No. 668 of 2025 on exam cheating.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: UAE federal education ministry's binding rules on generative AI use in school classrooms (sectoral, generative-ai).

instruments.official_title: Practical Guidance Note No. 2 of 2023 Guidelines on the use of large language models and generative AI in proceedings before the DIFC Courts
instruments.english_title: DIFC Courts Practical Guidance Note No. 2 of 2023 on large language models and generative AI in proceedings
instruments.current_status: Issued 21 December 2023 and in effect from that date (cited as PGN 2/2023). The note describes itself as guidance; it applies to parties and practitioners in proceedings before the DIFC Courts.
instruments.summary: Sets out how parties and practitioners before the DIFC Courts should use large language models and generative content generators in proceedings. It asks them to disclose AI use early, verify AI-generated content against independent sources, protect client confidentiality and avoid over-reliance, and reminds them that the Courts may reject AI-generated content and that false statements of truth can lead to contempt proceedings.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Court guidance on generative AI use in litigation in the DIFC.
instruments.evidence_reference: DIFC Courts practice directions page for PGN 2/2023, read 2026-10-18: date line "December 21, 2023"; section 2 "will come into effect from 21 December 2023"; sections 3-4 principles and best practices.

instruments.official_title: قانون رقم (3) لسنة 2024 بإنشاء مجلس الذكاء الاصطناعي والتكنولوجيا المتقدمة
instruments.english_title: Abu Dhabi Law No. (3) of 2024 establishing the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council
instruments.current_status: Issued 22 January 2024 and in force from that date (Article 12); published in the Abu Dhabi Official Gazette, Issue 1, Year 53, dated 31 January 2024. Repealed by Law No. (5) of 2025 issued 13 October 2025; regulations and decisions made under it stay in force until replaced.
instruments.summary: Established the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council as an independent body reporting to the Ruler of Abu Dhabi and made it the highest authority for AI and advanced-technology projects, investment and research in the emirate. The Council was tasked with setting AI strategies and policies, conditions and standards for AI investment and research, and proposing AI legislation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding law of the Abu Dhabi AI governance body (now repealed and replaced).
instruments.evidence_reference: Abu Dhabi Official Gazette Issue 1/2024 (31 January 2024), contents page and pp. 16-21: Articles 1-4 (definitions, establishment, powers), Article 12 (in force from issue), signature date 22 January 2024.

instruments.official_title: قانون رقم (5) لسنة 2025 بشأن إعادة تنظيم مجلس الذكاء الاصطناعي والتكنولوجيا المتقدمة
instruments.english_title: Abu Dhabi Law No. (5) of 2025 reorganising the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council
instruments.current_status: Issued 13 October 2025 and in force from that date (Article 16); published in the Abu Dhabi Official Gazette, Issue 10, Year 54, dated 31 October 2025. Repeals Law No. (3) of 2024.
instruments.summary: Reorganises the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council as the highest authority for AI and advanced-technology projects, investment and research in Abu Dhabi, with powers to set AI strategies and policies, set conditions and standards for AI investment and research, propose AI legislation and approve strategic AI companies. Government and non-government entities in the AI sector must implement the systems, strategies, policies and decisions the Council adopts and provide it with information.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current founding law of the Abu Dhabi AI governance body.

instruments.official_title: Practice Direction 2 - Commercial and Civil Claims
instruments.english_title: ADGM Courts Practice Direction 2 - Commercial and Civil Claims (use of artificial intelligence in disclosure searches)
instruments.current_status: AI provision present in the edition dated 17 Oct 2025 (Practice Direction 2 re-issued on 17 October 2025); the date paragraphs 2.84-2.85 were first added is not officially published. The ADGM Courts Practice Directions as a set came into force on 30 May 2016. It applies to commercial and civil claims before the ADGM Courts.
instruments.summary: The ADGM Courts' practice direction on commercial and civil claims, made by the Chief Justice under the ADGM Court Procedure Rules 2016. Its AI provisions are paragraphs 2.84-2.85 on further or specific disclosure: a party's document search is not unreasonable just because it used artificial intelligence such as predictive coding, and a party that intends to use AI in a document search must tell all other parties and give enough detail of the search parameters.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Court rule requiring parties to disclose the use of AI in disclosure searches in ADGM proceedings.
metadata_gaps: Date paragraphs 2.84-2.85 were first added is not officially published; publication_date is the date of the edition that contains them (re-issued 17 October 2025)
Effective date of the AI provision not stated
instruments.evidence_reference: ADGM Courts PD 2 PDF (52 pages), read 2026-10-18: cover "Date re-issued: 17 October 2025"; para 2.84 a search "shall not be considered to be unreasonable solely because that party has used artificial intelligence"; para 2.85 the party "must inform all other parties of that intention and provide sufficient details of the parameters of the search". adgm.com listing: Practice Directions "came into force on 30 May 2016".

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Federal bodies, the emirates of Dubai and Abu Dhabi (including the Dubai International Financial Centre) and the national ministries were searched. No national adoption of the ISO/IEC AI standards was found, and several ministries had no AI document of their own. Some official sites were unavailable, so several items, including documents on the federal legislation portal and the health ministry's site, are held as leads until an official text is available.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 6 October 2026, covering federal bodies and the emirates of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, including the Dubai International Financial Centre. The UAE AI Office and the Cyber Security Council websites could not be read automatically, so details of the Council's AI security policy were taken from the government's official policy portal. Some documents are held as pending until an official text is published, including an autonomous-vehicles law and Abu Dhabi Global Market data protection rules due for a later sectoral pass. No national adoption of the ISO/IEC AI standards was found.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06 including an emirate-level pass (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, DIFC). ai.gov.ae and csc.gov.ae block automated reading; metadata for the Cyber Security Council AI policy taken from the u.ae policy page. Not recorded: Responsible Metaverse Self-governance Framework and Blockchain Guide (not AI governance); Dubai Law No. 9 of 2023 on autonomous vehicles and ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (to add in a sectoral follow-up); AI Maturity Self-Assessment Tool (tool, not a document). Standards: no UAE national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 or 5339 found. Several items are held as leads pending an official document. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 1 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education: Safe and Responsible Use Guide of Generative AI in Classrooms 2026 (recorded); National AI Literacy Curriculum Framework K-12 2026 (lead, scope borderline); Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research: workshops and Microsoft partnership only; no AI policy document found; Ministry of Health and Prevention: National Policy for the Promotion of Smart Health Services and AI in the UAE Health Sector, 18 May 2026 (recorded, located only: portal blocked); draft health AI ethical framework and planned federal health-AI law (leads); Ministry of Justice: AI page (national strategy link, MoJ AI services) and publications checked; Guiding Principles for AI Systems in Law Firms, Sept 2026 (lead, no official text); Ministry of Defence: nothing found; Ministry of Finance: AI procurement guidelines already held as a lead; 2027-2029 strategic plan with AI projects (internal plan, not recorded); Federal Tax Authority: internal AI strategy/tools only, nothing recorded; Ministry of Interior (incl. ICP, police): AI training programme only; nothing found; Ministry of Foreign Affairs: International Stance on AI Policy already recorded (Ministry of Cabinet Affairs); nothing new; Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation: AI-automated services only; nothing found; Ministry of Climate Change and Environment: IBM partnership / AI lab only; nothing found; Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure: nothing found; Ministry of Economy / Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology: nothing found; Ministry of Culture: nothing found (media AI guide already recorded under the AI Office); Ministry of Community Empowerment / Family / Sports / Tolerance: nothing found; Ministry of Cabinet Affairs / Prime Minister's Office: already recorded (AI Adoption Guideline, International Stance); UAE Government Media Office: Guide to Agentic AI Applications for Government Communication Teams, Sept 2026 (lead, no official text); Federal Authority for Government Human Resources: 2020 HR AI plan and SHL MoU only; nothing recorded. Not reached: none. Could not verify: uaelegislation.gov.ae (Cloudflare 403) and mohap.gov.ae (TLS reset / 503) could not be read.; Exact launch day of the MoE generative AI classroom guide (news reports say February 2026; document states only 2026)..

Gulf benchmark 2026-10-18: Added DIFC Courts PGN No. 2 of 2023 (i-298e65b084d2, judiciary, Dubai (DIFC), date and effect 21 December 2023 from the DIFC Courts page); Abu Dhabi Law No. 3 of 2024 (i-481e3ea7e2d3, issued 22 Jan 2024, Gazette Issue 1/2024 dated 31 Jan 2024, repealed) and Law No. 5 of 2025 (i-063ed60ba1a9, issued 13 Oct 2025, Gazette Issue 10/2025 dated 31 Oct 2025), both read in the Abu Dhabi Official Gazette PDFs on abudhabi.gov.ae; AIATC lead removed after promotion. Federal AI and Data Authority: uaecabinet.ae page of 14 June 2026 read (official name "Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority"); uaelegislation.gov.ae listing (site updated 16/10/2026) shows no 2026 federal law or decree-law (newest is Federal Decree-Law 33 of 2025); its search and year filters did not apply in headless reads, so the lead stays. World events added: Regulatory Intelligence Office (14 April 2025, uaecabinet.ae), AI and Data Authority approval (14 June 2026), DIFC PGN effect, Abu Dhabi laws. Courts: ADGM Courts practice directions list checked; no AI-specific direction, but PD 2 (re-issued 17 October 2025) paras 2.84-2.85 regulate AI use in disclosure searches (held as a lead pending scope decision). Dubai Courts site (dc.gov.ae) timed out; no Dubai Courts AI rule read. Lead "100 Practical Applications and Use Cases of Generative AI" not deleted: record i-6a95fff66327 is the separate media-sector guide. Year-only dates: no full date found for the national strategy (ai.gov.ae blocked), AI Adoption Guideline (PDF undated, re-read), CSC AI security policy (csc.gov.ae PDF TLS failure; u.ae page shows only "Updated on 02 Jul 2026") or the two MoE 2026 documents (MoE page lists no dates); all left unchanged. Gulf follow-up 2026-10-18: ADGM Courts Practice Direction 2 (re-issued 17 October 2025) promoted from lead to i-374216c055b3 after reading the PDF on assets.adgm.com; paras 2.84-2.85 use "must inform", so classed administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope; publication_date is the 30 May 2016 in-force date of the Practice Directions set printed on adgm.com (the PDF prints only the re-issue date); lead removed.
